# Salam

> Salam is a compiled, statically typed programming language whose keywords
> exist in English, Persian and Arabic. It compiles to native code through an
> LLVM or C backend, to JavaScript for the browser, and ships a large standard
> library (55 packages) plus a self-hosted compiler written in Salam itself.

The fastest way for a model to work with Salam is the MCP server in
`tools/mcp`, which exposes the compiler and the standard library as tools.
Point an MCP client at the `salam-mcp` binary and call `salam_check` after
every edit instead of guessing whether code compiles.

## Start here

- [Language guide for AI agents](AGENTS.md): syntax, the enforced declaration
  ordering rules, and the toolchain traps that silently produce wrong
  behaviour. Read this before writing any Salam.
- [Standard library index](stdlib-index.json): every importable `std` package
  mapped to its public declarations, generated from the source tree.
- [MCP server](../../tools/mcp/README.md): setup, tool reference, and the
  environment variables that scope it to a workspace.

## Source of truth

- `std/`: the standard library; every package is ordinary Salam source and is
  the authoritative reference for its own API.
- `tests/en`, `tests/fa`, `tests/ar`: the test corpus, and the largest body of
  known-good Salam in the repository.
- `compiler/`: the self-hosted compiler, written in Salam.
- `c/src/langpack/langpack_data.c`: the English/Persian/Arabic keyword tables.
